previous_attempt_summaries.strategy_summary: Reduce the coloring statement to a structural theorem about a single color class viewed as a subset of the plane that is closed under taking circumcenters of noncollinear triples. Then prove that some color class must contain a noncollinear triple, and invoke the structural theorem to conclude that this color class is the whole plane.

previous_attempt_summaries.strategy_summary: Reformulate the hypothesis as a closure property for each color class, then combine two external geometric-combinatorial facts: (i) any 2-coloring of the Euclidean plane contains a monochromatic equilateral triangle, and (ii) any nonempty subset of the plane that is closed under taking circumcenters of noncollinear triples is either contained in a line or equals the whole plane. The monochromatic equilateral triangle rules out the 'contained in a line' case, forcing one color class to be all of R^2.
previous_attempt_summaries.vet_summary: Fatal flaw: the central structural lemmas L4 and L5 are false. A concrete counterexample is S = Q^2, which is nonempty, not contained in any line, and closed under circumcenters of noncollinear triples with rational coordinates, but S != R^2. The assembly is logically complete only conditional on those lemmas. L4 is also redundant in the stated assembly because only L5 is invoked.

shared_context.content: The Euclidean plane is identified with R^2. For three noncollinear points A,B,C, write circumcenter(A,B,C) for the unique point equidistant from A,B,C. If three distinct points lie on a circle with center O, then circumcenter(A,B,C)=O.
shared_context.label: SC1

shared_context.content: A 2-coloring is a function f : R^2 -> {red, green}. The root hypothesis is: for all noncollinear A,B,C in R^2, if f(A)=f(B)=f(C), then f(circumcenter(A,B,C))=f(A).
shared_context.label: SC2

strategy_summary: Use a point-to-point color-transfer argument built from two specific opposite-colored points and a finite family of auxiliary circles. This differs from the failed attempts by avoiding any false global classification of circumcenter-closed subsets such as 'noncollinear implies all of R^2'; every structural step here explicitly uses the 2-coloring hypothesis and the chosen centers O and G.
